sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Duplin County?
sections.html:
Duplin County deeds are filed at 118 Duplin Street in Kenansville, in the Register of Deeds office, which opens at 8 am and closes at 5 pm Monday to Friday. Call 910-296-2108 with questions; the fax line is 910-296-2344, and mail can go to Box 970, Kenansville, NC 28349.

The county dates the office to the organization of county government in 1750. Besides deeds, the staff handle the following:

  • Deeds of trust and powers of attorney.
  • Assumed business names and military records.
  • Maps and plats.
  • Notary commissions and marriage licenses.
  • Certified copies of vital records.

Real property records, vital records and maps are searchable online, and the county points visitors to duplinrod.com. The county's recommended 2026-27 budget shows five positions in the office and about $499,896 recommended for it, and it sets aside a small automation and preservation fund, budgeted at $25,000, that draws on part of the fees the office collects.

sections.h2: What does registering a Duplin County deed protect?
sections.html:
A deed protects its holder against outsiders only once it is on the public record. G.S. 47-18 says a deed, a contract to convey, an option, a lease running more than three years, or a first-refusal right cannot defeat lien creditors or paying purchasers until it is registered where the land lies.

If two documents compete, the earlier registration wins. That is why a buyer cannot treat a signed but unfiled deed as finished, and why sellers should ask the closing attorney when filing will happen.

Tax-side ownership data lives with Land Records inside the Duplin tax department, so call that office after closing to see when the new owner shows on the account.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees at the Duplin County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
One schedule governs every county, set by G.S. 161-10, and the register collects it before filing.

Statewide recording charges under G.S. 161-10, payable at the Duplin County Register of Deeds
DocumentCharge printed in the statute
General instrument such as a deed$26.00 covers 15 pages; each added page is $4.00
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 covers 35 pages; each added page is $4.00
Plat$21.00 a sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each page after
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo charge

Two add-ons appear in the same statute: $25.00 for a nonstandard document and $10.00 for each extra instrument in one filing. Page count drives the total, so count before mailing.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed stamp tax in Duplin County?
sections.html:
The grantor pays. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the levy at a dollar per five hundred dollars of consideration, rounding any remainder up, collected at the register's counter ahead of recording.

  • The county general fund receives half.
  • The remaining half goes to the state, and the county keeps 2% of that share as a collection allowance.
  • A tract spread over several counties pays where most of its value lies.

Let the closing attorney work out the stamp for your price, since the register takes the tax before accepting the deed.

sections.h2: How do I coordinate a Duplin County deed with the tax office?
sections.html:
The register records the deed; the Duplin County Tax Department at 117 Beasley Street bills the tax. Collections answers at 910-296-2112, and the assessing office at 910-296-2110.

Tax comes due September 1, and interest starts on January 6, so a closing in autumn or winter has a live bill attached to it. On delinquent accounts the tax office sends the file to the county attorney, and foreclosure sales take place on the courthouse steps in Kenansville, where the top bidder leaves a 20% deposit.

Phone Collections for a payoff ahead of closing. If the parcel lies in Calypso, Greenevers, Kenansville, Magnolia, Rose Hill, Teachey, Wallace or Warsaw, the county also collects that town's levy, so the payoff should include it.

sections.h2: What steps get a Duplin County deed recorded?
sections.html:
The register will not file a document until the money is in, so the order of steps matters.

  1. Obtain a payoff from Collections so the year's tax and any back balance are cleared at the table.
  2. Have the deed drawn up and signed.
  3. Pay the deed stamp, then add the page-based fee from the table.
  4. Deliver the document to 118 Duplin Street or mail it to Box 970.
  5. If a lender asks for a certified copy later, expect the statutory per-page charge shown in the table.

With an inherited house, settle who may sign for the estate before anything is drafted. The register files the paper without ruling on that, so speak with the clerk of superior court and an attorney first.

sections.h2: Do owner-financed sales get recorded in Duplin County?
sections.html:
Yes, and Chapter 47H adds rules. It reaches written agreements with five or more payments after the down payment, where the seller keeps title, on one-to-four family dwellings or manufactured homes priced at $5,000 or more.

  • Paper, signatures and an acknowledgment are all required.
  • The buyer may rescind up to midnight ending the third business day after execution or delivery.
  • Five business days is the seller's window to record the contract itself or a short memorandum of it.
  • A forfeiture begins with a written default notice giving at least 30 days to cure.

A seller who forgets to record loses the protection described above, so put it on the closing checklist.

sections.h2: Which Duplin County towns and roads do these deeds cover?
sections.html:
The register serves a county of about 819 square miles, bordered by Wayne, Lenoir, Jones, Onslow, Pender and Sampson counties. Kenansville, the county seat, sits roughly in the middle, where NC 24, NC 11 and NC 50 meet, and Interstate 40 and US 117 run through the wider county.

Beulaville, Calypso, Faison, Greenevers, Magnolia, Rose Hill, Teachey, Wallace and Warsaw are the other municipalities the county names. A deed for a house in any of them, or in the rural land between them, is recorded in the same Kenansville office. The county's own budget message calls Duplin a rural county leaning on agriculture and industry, with little retail growth.

sections.h2: How do Duplin County tax rates and revaluation shape a sale?
sections.html:
A deed transfers the house, but the tax bill moves with the calendar. Duplin's county rate in the recommended 2026-27 budget is 58 cents per $100, and fire districts add their own rates. The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2025, and the next is set for January 1, 2030.

The 2025 revaluation lifted the county tax base by about 25%, and the county reported reaching roughly 98 percent of market value. For a seller, that means the assessed value on the bill is already close to market value, which helps when a buyer's lender asks about the tax load. The tax office reported 42,374 nonexempt parcels as of January 2026.

sections.h2: What do Duplin County housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts puts Duplin at 51,571 people and 24,235 housing units in July 2025, with owners in 70.3% of homes, spread over 814.72 square miles of land.

Median owner-occupied value was $137,400 for 2020-2024; median rent was $865 and median household income $55,148. Permits for new building totaled 127 in 2025.

faqs.q: What hours does the Duplin County Register of Deeds keep?
faqs.a: It is open Monday to Friday, 8 am until 5 pm, at 118 Duplin Street, and the number to call is 910-296-2108.

faqs.q: What will recording my Duplin County deed cost?
faqs.a: The statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10 starts at $26.00 for a short deed and $64.00 for a deed of trust, with $4.00 more for each page beyond the included count.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for the excise tax on a Duplin County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does, at the register's counter before recording, one dollar per five hundred dollars of value.

faqs.q: Are Duplin County deeds searchable online?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says most public records, including real property, vital records and maps, can be searched through the register's website at duplinrod.com.

faqs.q: Does recording the deed clear the Duplin County property tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Tax is billed and collected by the Duplin County Tax Department and is due each September 1, so request a payoff from Collections at 910-296-2112 before closing.
